questions.question: Which statement correctly separates replication from sharding?
options: Replication divides keys among owners, while sharding stores copies of each key
Replication copies an ownership range, while sharding divides keys into ownership ranges
Replication always scales writes, while sharding only improves durability
They are two names for the same database operation
questions.explanation: Replication stores copies of the same range. Sharding partitions different keys into ownership ranges. A sharded production database often replicates every shard.

questions.question: What problem does consistent hashing primarily solve?
options: Encrypting keys before storage
Limiting ownership changes when the node set changes
Making every write strongly consistent
Detecting failed nodes without heartbeats
questions.explanation: Consistent hashing is a placement technique. It keeps most key-to-owner mappings stable when one owner joins or leaves.

questions.question: What is the core on-disk invariant of an SSTable?
options: Records are mutable and stored in insertion order
Records are immutable and sorted by key
Every key has a full in-memory index entry
Every write immediately updates all levels
questions.explanation: An SSTable is written once and keeps records in key order. Immutability enables sequential creation and checksums; sorting enables sparse indexes and ordered scans.

questions.question: A telemetry table uses PRIMARY KEY ((tenant_id), event_time). One tenant produces most of the writes. What is the central risk?
options: Clustering by event_time automatically spreads the tenant across token owners
All of that tenant's writes still target one logical partition and its replica set
Increasing the replication factor splits the partition into independent shards
The coordinator permanently becomes the primary for that tenant
questions.explanation: The partition key, not the clustering column, determines the token and replica set. Replication makes copies of the same hot partition; it does not subdivide the key.

questions.question: Which statement correctly describes DynamoDB's core data model?
options: A table contains items, and each item is a collection of attributes
A table contains joins, and each join owns a partition
Every item in a table must declare the same non-key attributes
A sort key chooses the AWS Region for an item
questions.explanation: A DynamoDB table contains items, and each item contains attributes. Only the primary-key attributes are required by the table schema; other attributes can differ between items.
